_comment: Append-only log. Current status per (subject, control_id) is its most recent entry. This is what closes this tool's own NIST-MANAGE gap (finding found -> tracked -> resolved), not just a static remediation list.

entries.subject: portfolio-sync
entries.note: Initial finding from the first crosswalk run: no technical documentation package exists beyond the operational system prompt and GOVERNANCE.md's policy notes.

entries.subject: portfolio-sync
entries.note: Flagged for human review, not a confirmed gap: whether Article 10 (training-data governance) meaningfully applies to a non-trained agent system is an open interpretive question, not something resolved unilaterally.

entries.subject: portfolio-sync
entries.note: Initial finding: real Manage-relevant activity happened (classifier negation-blindness bug found and fixed between the 07-23 and 08-04 red-team runs) but was never tracked as such until this crosswalk's GOVERNANCE.md backfill.

entries.subject: do178c-build-test
entries.note: Initial finding: no training/validation/testing dataset exists for this build/test orchestration agent, and unlike portfolio-sync there's no live-data-governance analog either. Same open interpretive question on whether Article 10 applies at all.

entries.subject: do178c-build-test
entries.note: Initial finding: same pattern as portfolio-sync's NIST-MANAGE gap — real fix activity happened but was never tracked as such.

entries.subject: portfolio-sync
entries.note: Resolved by reading EU AI Act Article 3 (Definitions) directly. Article 10 governs training/validation/testing data (Art. 3(29)-(32)) — data used to fit or tune an AI model's parameters. portfolio-sync only supplies 'input data' (Art. 3(33)) to an already-trained general-purpose AI model; it never trains or tunes anything. Training-data governance for the underlying model is Anthropic's obligation as its provider (Chapter V), not this system's. Coverage updated Partial -> Met in findings/portfolio-sync-findings.json (nothing left ungoverned, since the requirement's precondition doesn't apply here). Secondary finding: Art. 3(4)'s deployer definition excludes 'personal non-professional activity,' which this likely is — noted as context, doesn't change the verdict.

entries.subject: do178c-build-test
entries.note: Resolved on the same basis as portfolio-sync's EU-ART10 entry above. Coverage updated Gap -> Met in findings/do178c-build-test-findings.json.

entries.subject: self-learning-agent
entries.note: Initial finding from the third crosswalk subject's first run: self-learning-agent was never added to ai-security/GOVERNANCE.md, so no canonical governance section exists for it. The substance largely exists in the project blueprint (accountable party, standing no-autonomous-write rule) but hasn't been captured in the place this tool and ai-security both look for it.

entries.subject: self-learning-agent
entries.note: Resolved same day as the initial finding: added a real Govern section to ai-security/GOVERNANCE.md covering the accountable party, the structurally-enforced confirmation gate, the DOM-tool-wins-over-MCP standing rule, and the red-team validation under adversarial pressure. Coverage updated Gap -> Met in findings/self-learning-agent-findings.json. One item remains explicitly unformalized (incident response if the gate is ever bypassed), same as the other two subjects' open items — not treated as blocking this resolution.

entries.subject: portfolio-sync
entries.note: Resolved by writing a real Annex IV-style technical documentation package (ai-security/targets/portfolio_sync_technical_documentation.md) covering general description, design/development process with rationale per real key choice, monitoring/human-oversight measures, and a risk-management section grounded in the actual red-team results and the classifier defect found and fixed. Wired into evidence.py as a real evidence source (SUBJECT_TECH_DOC_FILES), not just referenced. Coverage updated Gap -> Met in findings/portfolio-sync-findings.json. Flagged needs_human_review: true (confidence: medium) rather than closed unilaterally — whether a personal-system-scoped package satisfies Article 11 the way a full commercial-product package would is a real interpretive judgment, same category as the EU-ART10 resolution above, not a mechanical check. Two elements explicitly marked not-applicable rather than omitted: harmonised standards (none exist for this system class) and declaration of conformity (no EU market placement).
